title: operator-onboard-cookbook-session-slices-and-query-throttle-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operator onboarding cookbook for session-slice mapping, lightweight dashboard staging, and query-throttle patterns used during bursty inference incidents. The doc is intentionally informal — meant to live in Drive as the playbook we iterate on while practising runbooks in tabletop drills.

Audience:
- Oncall operators (new hires and rotating engineers)
- SREs and owners of inference dashboards
- Feature owners who want minimal-cost telemetry for rollouts

Goals (what success looks like):
1) New operator can reconstruct a user session and triage a slow-token incident within 15 minutes using the compact dashboard.
2) Dashboards only surface high-signal slices; median query cost of investigation < 10 USD per incident.
3) Traces sampled enough to anchor latency regressions but bounded by budgeted trace tokens.

Quick glossary (how we use terms here):
- session-slice: a lightweight bucket used to group related requests for debugging (e.g. tenant+route+kv-warmth-bucket).
- compact dashboard: single-screen operator view with 6 widgets (sli ladder, heatmap, error-table, sample trace links, cost-quickcard, top-ten tenants).
- investigation token budget: ceiling for ad-hoc queries during an incident (default daily 2000 tokens for ops).

Decision matrix (current conventions):
- Slicing keys (default order): tenant_id > route_name > model_variant > kv_warmth_bucket. Keep cardinality at most 200k for metrics ingestion.
- Trace sampling: 1% global + 5% of requests with latency > p95 for the route. For canaries, enable verbose traces at 10% for 48 hours.
- Dashboard staging: every dashboard goes through "compact -> expanded -> archived" lifecycle. Compact dashboards are the only ones allowed in oncall quicklinks.

Metric definitions (compact forms for operators):
- op.session_request_count: "count of incoming inference requests grouped by session_slice"; cardinality: low (slice key only); owner: eng-observability; query hint: sum(count) by slice over 1m.
- op.token_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99: "per-token generation latency quantiles"; cardinality: route+model_variant; note: instrument at runtime exit path.
- op.kv_cache_hit_ratio: "fraction of requests that used a non-empty KV cache prefix"; cardinality: route; owner: solutions-engineering.
- op.prefix_replay_rate: "requests that triggered prefix replay (cache miss leading to cold-start)"; cardinality: route+tenant_class; alert if > 0.05 sustained 5m.
- cost.investigation_query_cost_usd: "ad-hoc query cost accrued by ops queries"; cardinality: operator_id; purpose: keep investigations under budget.

Tracing annotations (what to capture on spans):
- span tags: tenant_id, route, model_variant, request_id, session_id (if available), kv_cache_state (HIT/MISS/COLD), batch_size, seq_len_tokens.
- event markers: prefix-load-start, kv-lookup-end, response-write-start, model-call-return.
- span duration breakouts: tokenize_ms, model_infer_ms, kv_lookup_ms, postproc_ms.

Compact dashboard layout (operator quick view):
Top row (context): small card: active-oncalls, current incident id, investigation token budget left.
Left column (traffic & slices):
  - Live slice heatmap (rows: tenant buckets, cols: routes) colored by p95 token latency.
  - Slice trend sparkline (select slice -> 30m/6h/24h).
Center (investigation):
  - SLI ladder (p50/p95/p99 for selected slice, plus delta vs baseline).
  - Recent error table (error class, count, sample request link).
Right (triage helpers):
  - Top 3 sample traces (click to open trace viewer).
  - Query-cost quickcard (queries run in this incident, USD).
  - Runbook links + suggested next steps (canary rollback, dial-up cache priming, scale policy).

Dashboard staging checklist (for dashboard owners):
- [ ] Does the compact dashboard fit on one 1366x768 screen without scrolling?
- [ ] All widgets bound by default to a 30m window; can be expanded.
- [ ] Widgets use aggregated cardinalities; no metric emits high-cardinality labels (no raw user text).
- [ ] Linked traces include sampling id + repro prompt (masked).
- [ ] Cost quickcard shows cumulative query tokens and estimated USD with breakdown by operator query type.
- [ ] Owner and rotation listed in dashboard metadata.

Alerting & thresholds (practical defaults):
- Route-level latency alert: p95 > baseline+40% sustained 5m -> sev2.
- Slice-level cold-starts: prefix_replay_rate > 5% over 10m -> paging to SRE oncall if slice traffic > 1rps.
- Investigation-budget alert: cost.investigation_query_cost_usd > daily_budget*0.9 -> notify oncall lead, stop non-critical ad-hoc queries.
- Trace-budget guard: sampling tokens used > trace_budget_daily -> reduce global sampling to 0.1% automatically (fallback).

Query-throttle patterns (how operators should limit exploratory queries):
- Use sample -> filter -> aggregate pattern: start with a small sample (LIMIT 500) of request_ids, reconstruct sessions locally, then run aggregated queries.
- Prefab queries: we maintain a set of 8 approved investigation queries (see linked_artifacts). Use these before writing custom SQL.
- If you need high-cardinality extraction (e.g. full prompt), escalate to a privacy-approved channel and capture only hashed keys.

Oncall play examples (short run-throughs):
1) P95 spike on /generate for tenant X:
   - Open compact dashboard -> filter tenant_id=X -> see heatmap row -> check kv_cache_hit_ratio for route.
   - If kv_cache_hit_ratio drastically low & prefix_replay_rate high: likely cold-starts -> trigger cache-priming job, open ticket for platform to review cache sizing.
   - If kv_cache_hit_ratio normal but model_infer_ms elevated: open model route traces, check batch_size and seq_len distribution.
2) Costly investigations:
   - If cost quickcard shows spend trending > budget, pause ad-hoc trace exports and switch to aggregated queries only. Notify incident lead.

Open questions / TODOs:
- We still need a low-cost session-id propagation shim for SDKs to improve reconstruction fidelity. (owner: devexp, ETA: Q2).
- Define a canonical tenant bucket mapping strategy for customers with >10K tenants to avoid cardinality explosions. (owner: eng-platform).
- Run a 48h trial of the proposed trace-sampling law that biases for long tail (p95) and canaries. (owner: SRE).

References / bookmarks:
- Confluence: OBS-operator-onboarding (linked_artifacts)
- Jira: OBS-3421 (dashboard-staging)
- Slack thread: #observability-ops (thread-id above)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and link to deeper design papers that live in Confluence.
- During drills, have new oncall try the compact dashboard flow and time them. Capture where they get stuck and iterate.

If you're reading this and want to add a brick: please add one concrete example trace (anonymized) under "linked_artifacts" so operators can practise without hitting prod.
